clue.text: Fit to crack up?

parts.note: 'fit' is read as deserving or worthy, and 'crack up' as to speak highly of, so the phrase means deserving of acclaim rather than likely to break down

explanation.surface: Someone is so stressed they look ready to have a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack up' looks like collapsing in laughter or nerves, but 'cracked up' also means highly spoken of, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of being lauded is deserving of commendation.

clue.text: Language encountered in bar, one opened by Jack in North America

indicators.note: the bar and the one are split open by what follows, so those letters sit inside them

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: Jack goes in, so its letter sits between the letters for North America

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A language heard spoken in a bar somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened by' splits the bar-and-one pair after its second letter to take in Jack within North America; 'encountered in' just links. Jack is the card abbreviation J.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Left millions to be invested, in the form of charitable donations

indicators.note: invested here means wrapped or clothed in, so these letters are placed inside the next piece

parts.note: as means in the form of, as in 'dressed as a pirate'
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a fortune in their will to be invested for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' looks financial; it means placed inside, so L and M go into AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts of money or food handed to the poor are traditionally called alms.

clue.text: Evening hour by which three card players must accept ruin

indicators.note: the card players take in the ruin, so its letters go inside theirs

parts.note: at bridge the four players are named by compass points; South, West and North give S, W and N
to undo someone is to ruin them

explanation.surface: Three bridge players agree to stop by evening or face ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, North, South, East and West; 'must accept' has three of them take in the word for ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: The time when the sun sets marks the start of evening.

clue.text: Bits of ironmongery belonged to the woman

parts.note: belonged to someone means it was theirs, giving the verb was
belonging to the woman is hers

explanation.surface: Some hardware items were the property of a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'belonged to the woman' as the phrase 'was hers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Washers are flat rings used with nuts and bolts, sold by hardware shops.

clue.text: Horse cantered round ring

indicators.note: the run word goes round the ring, so the ring's letter sits inside it

parts.note: cantered means moved quickly, ran
a ring is O-shaped, giving O

explanation.surface: A horse went cantering round the show ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cantered' suggests a horse in the scene, but here it just means RAN, which goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat mixes white hairs with a base colour.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman, one happy to be put up in house

indicators.note: the pieces go in the house, so their letters sit inside its abbreviation

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in a down entry put up means written upwards, so the word for happy is read backwards

parts.note: glad means happy

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman, pleased to be a guest staying in someone's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' looks like being given a bed; it is the reversal, turning GLAD to DALG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of the lower Spanish nobility.

clue.text: Gather bottles clashing may be source of loud noise

indicators.note: the letters collide and fall into a new order, as clashing things jumble together

explanation.surface: Collecting empty bottles that clink together can be very noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clashing' rearranges the letters of GATHER BOTTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A large portable stereo, famous for blaring music in the street in the 1980s.

clue.text: Procedure in which the majority may be to blame?

definitions.text: Procedure in which the majority may be to blame?

parts.words: Procedure in which the majority may be to blame?
parts.note: read as a formal ballot where most members decide that someone is at fault, rather than a crowd being guilty

explanation.surface: Wondering whether most people are responsible for some failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The majority may be to blame' sounds like most people being guilty; it means most voters finding someone guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ballot in parliament or a body declaring disapproval of a leader or government.

clue.text: Ketch maybe starts for home after nearing Greek island

indicators.note: the starts of these four words are taken, their first letters

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A ketch, a sailing boat, heads home after approaching a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ketch' looks like a two-masted boat; Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English executioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch was an infamous public executioner, an example of someone who carries out sentences of death.

clue.text: Boy receiving a medal, an unpleasant person

indicators.note: the boy takes in the a, so its letter goes inside his

parts.note: a son is a boy
the DSO, Distinguished Service Order, is a British military decoration

explanation.surface: A lad is awarded a medal, yet he is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The DSO (Distinguished Service Order) is a British military award; 'receiving' puts the A inside the boy, between his second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a so-and-so is a mild way of naming a disliked individual.

clue.text: Vehicle in which constituent returns

indicators.note: the word for constituent comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: a constituent is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: A voter is driven back home in some vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' looks like a voter; here it means a component, PART, written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a horse.

clue.text: Style evident in poem written in 1050

indicators.note: the poem is inscribed inside the number, so its letters sit within the numerals

parts.note: in Roman numerals 1000 is M and 50 is L
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A style of verse can be seen in a poem composed in the year 1050.
explanation.walkthrough: 1050 looks like a date; split it into Roman M (1000) and L (50) and put ODE between.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a particular design or version, as in a car's latest style.

clue.text: Left in charge, move off quickly

indicators.note: left goes in the charge, its letter sitting inside the word

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: Someone left minding things decides to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' reads as responsible; split it so 'charge' is FEE with L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away hastily from danger.

clue.text: finds a face-saver

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'finds a face-saver (5)': the clue is cut short at the start; VISOR fits 'face-saver' but the wordplay that 'finds' it is missing, and no search found the full clue

clue.text: Ambassador, old, steeped in sin

indicators.note: the old is soaked inside the sin, so its letter sits within that word

parts.note: envy is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: An elderly diplomat thoroughly immersed in wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside ENVY, between V and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a diplomatic representative sent abroad.

clue.text: Work in Scottish island, mostly for the view

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
taken as written

indicators.note: most of the island's name is used, dropping its final letter

parts.note: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland

explanation.surface: Working on a Scottish island, largely for the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'View' looks like scenery, but it means a belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of a held belief or judgement.

clue.text: Dismiss striker, say?

parts.note: a referee showing a forward the red card dismisses that player from the field

explanation.surface: Getting rid of someone on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a worker on strike; it is a football forward being sent from the pitch, and the phrase also names a farewell party.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee's dismissal of a player, and also a farewell celebration.

clue.text: Employers' action making TUC look askance?

indicators.note: looking askance is looking awry, so the letters are set askew into a new order

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions

explanation.surface: Bosses do something that makes the trade unions frown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Askance' rearranges TUC LOOK; the TUC is the UK's trade union federation, fitting the industrial-dispute surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosses shutting workers out of the workplace is an industrial weapon used against unions.

clue.text: Rioting mob seen in half of state capital

indicators.note: the jumbled mob appears inside the shortened state, so its letters sit within
only the first half of the state's name is used

parts.note: Colorado is a US state

indicators.note: rioting means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A violent crowd appears in one half of a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rioting' scrambles the mob and 'seen in' places the result inside half of the state, Colorado; the capital is Sri Lanka's, not a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the commercial capital of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Paint a salesman 2

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Paint a salesman 2 (7)': A + REP gives only part of TEMPERA reversed; the clue's MET and reversal indicator are missing or garbled into '2', and no search found the full clue

clue.text: Doddery old butler in distress

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters totter into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly, unsteady manservant is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doddery' rearranges O and BUTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is a state of difficulty or distress.

clue.text: Regiment initially stood down is re-formed, present in large numbers

indicators.note: the remaining letters are formed again into a new arrangement
the first letter of regiment is stood down, taken away

explanation.surface: A regiment first stood down is reconstituted with many soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially stood down' drops the R of REGIMENT, and 'is re-formed' rearranges EGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means swarming or crowded with many.

clue.text: Oscar, child tucking into cheese roll

indicators.note: Oscar and the child go inside the cheese, as if eating into it

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boy named Oscar and a child eat a cheese roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' looks like eating, but it places Oscar and child inside the cheese; Oscar is O in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a sweet, rich French bread bun.

clue.text: Dispose of charm, reduced by a penny

indicators.note: the charm word is made shorter by taking out the penny

parts.note: a spell is a charm
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a lucky charm at a penny off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from SPELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell something is to get rid of it for money.

clue.text: Fossil found in Camberwell

indicators.note: the answer is discovered lying within the letters of the place name

explanation.surface: A fossil was discovered in the London district of Camberwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Camberwell is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin.

clue.text: Young lady from American state

explanation.surface: A girl from somewhere in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a title for an unmarried woman, and the short form of Mississippi.

clue.text: Notice later addition in old article that's turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means the whole piece is read upwards, from the bottom
the later addition goes in the old article, its letters sitting inside

parts.note: ye is an old form of the definite article 'the'
a PS, postscript, is added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Spotting an afterthought tucked into an old article that has surfaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts the postscript inside the old article, then 'turned up' reverses the whole result, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of.

clue.text: Notion one college fellow ultimately dismissed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the final letter of the college fellow is sent away

parts.note: a dean is a senior fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Thinking that a college academic was finally sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAN loses its last letter to give DEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or concept.

clue.text: Seamen milling around square in a body

indicators.note: the jumbled sailors go around the square's letter
milling means moving about in a confused crowd, so the letters swirl into new order

explanation.surface: Sailors mill about a town square as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SEAMEN, ENMASE, goes around S.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French for all together as a group.

clue.text: Vehicle, exciting one, state?

parts.note: read as a thrilling motor from Indiana, whose Indianapolis 500 race names a class of racing machine

explanation.surface: Asking about an exciting kind of car from a particular state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indianapolis 500 is a famous motor race in Indiana; its racing cars are known by the city's short name.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-wheel racing car of the type driven at Indianapolis.

clue.text: Unconsciously revealing points in speech to committee, perhaps?

definitions.text: Unconsciously revealing points in speech to committee, perhaps?

parts.words: Unconsciously revealing points in speech to committee, perhaps?
parts.note: read as the tongue spoken by a group such as a committee, a 'body', while really meaning gestures and posture that give away feelings

explanation.surface: Someone inadvertently gives away key points while addressing a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: A committee is a body, so its speech would be its 'language'; the phrase really means signals given by posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures and postures that communicate feelings without words.
